If you're reading this, you've probably already noticed it: a little more scalp than usual along your hairline, some tenderness after taking down a style, maybe a bald patch at the temples that wasn't there a few years ago. That's traction alopecia, and if it's from years of tight ponytails, braids, weaves, or ill-fitted extensions, you are far from alone. It's one of the most common reasons clients walk through our doors in Greenwich Village, and it's one of the most misunderstood.

What Traction Alopecia Actually Is

Traction alopecia develops when hair is pulled at the root, repeatedly and over time, until the follicle weakens and eventually stops producing hair altogether. It's most common along the hairline, temples, and part line — anywhere tension is concentrated. The good news is that caught early, it's often reversible. The bad news is that a lot of hair extensions actually make it worse, because the wrong method just adds more weight and more pull to already-stressed follicles.

That's the core issue we talk through with almost every client who comes to us specifically for hair extensions for traction alopecia: the goal isn't just to add hair, it's to add hair in a way that takes tension *off* the scalp instead of adding to it.

Why the Wrong Method Can Make Things Worse

Traditional sew-in weaves with tight braided tracks, heavy clip-ins worn daily, and glue-based extensions applied too close to the hairline are common culprits behind traction alopecia in the first place. So the last thing we want to do is recommend something that repeats the pattern. This is where an honest consultation matters more than almost anything else we offer.

The Extension Methods That Actually Help

For clients dealing with traction alopecia, we typically steer toward:

●        Natural Beaded Rows (hand-tied wefts): distribute weight across a wider area of the scalp rather than concentrating it at a few points, and can be installed to avoid the most affected zones entirely.

●        Microlink Extensions: applied with tiny, adjustable rings rather than heat or adhesive, which means we can control tension precisely and skip over any areas that are still healing.

●        Tape-In Extensions: lightweight and flat against the scalp, with far less pulling force than braided or glued methods, though placement near an active hairline recession needs a careful, experienced eye.

We source all of our extensions from 100% human Slavic hair, which is naturally fine in diameter — that matters here specifically, because finer strands mean less overall weight pulling on already-fragile follicles compared to coarser or synthetic alternatives.

Healing While You Wear Them

A good stylist doing this kind of work isn't just installing extensions and sending you home. We'll talk to you about scalp rest periods, how to sleep in your extensions without adding tension overnight, and when to come back in for adjustment rather than leaving something in too long. The goal is length and fullness *today*, without borrowing against your hairline tomorrow.

You Deserve an Honest Conversation, Not Just a Sale

If you've been told before that extensions "aren't an option" for traction alopecia, we'd gently push back on that. The right method, placed by someone who understands what your scalp has been through, can absolutely coexist with a healing hairline. What matters is that whoever is doing the placing actually knows the difference between adding hair and adding harm.

Every hair loss consultation at Luxe Aura Hair is private and unhurried — we'll look at your specific pattern of thinning, talk through what's realistic, and recommend a method (or tell you honestly if now isn't the time yet). You can book online or call us at (212) 221-3881.
